title: Section 8 Rent-Increase Deadline Capture Service
one_liner: A tracker that knows each voucher tenant's lease anniversary, sees the new FY2027 payment standard, and files the landlord's rent-increase request inside the tight 60-day window before a year of raise is forfeited.
customer: Small landlords with 1 to 50 Housing Choice Voucher units, especially out-of-state investors in Section 8-heavy markets such as Memphis, Cleveland, St. Louis and Indianapolis. Small PM firms with voucher portfolios are the second segment.
problem: Housing-authority payment standards rose for FY2027, but a new standard does not flow through to an existing tenancy on October 1. It applies only at each tenant's lease anniversary. The owner must send a written request within a typically tight window, often 60 days before that date, or forfeit the increase for a year. Each housing authority has its own forms and dates. Most small owners never map the anniversary dates, so they leave real money uncollected. One market analysis found 3-bedroom increases of 6 to 12%, with a median of 10%.
solution: The landlord uploads photos of their HAP contracts and leases, and the tool extracts tenant anniversary dates and current contract rents. The team maintains a database of housing-authority payment standards and each authority's request process (scraped from PHA PDFs and notices, human-verified). For each unit it computes the increase headroom, alerts at 90, 75 and 60 days before the window closes, and generates the authority-specific rent-increase request letter or form. It tracks proof of submission and logs who was contacted and when. It also flags likely mistakes in the original rent-reasonableness record (wrong bedroom count or square footage) that justify a correction request mid-lease.
why_now: FY2027 standards take effect around October 1, 2026, and today is 2026-09-28. Anniversary windows are opening across the country right now. The forum thread on this appeared within days, and the one-year forfeiture is a hard deadline that makes people spend money.
revenue_model: Success-aligned pricing: $5 per unit per month, plus 1 month of the captured increase for each unit where the request is approved. On a $1,300 rent and a 10% bump, that is $130 per month, or $1,560 a year, per unit. Authority data is the moat; a PM-firm plan can charge per door. Later, a similar deadline tracker can cover annual recertification and inspection dates.
non_obvious_insight: The money is lost to a calendar, not to the tenant or the market, and the people who feel it are the least likely to be organized. A BiggerPockets post titled 'Section 8 rents went up for FY2027. Most landlords won't collect it' says: 'A new payment standard does not flow through to an existing tenancy on October 1'. It adds that owners must submit written requests within a typically tight 60-day window before each anniversary or forfeit the opportunity for an entire year. It reports 3-bedroom rates up 6-12% (median 10%) in nine of ten low-cost ZIP codes, and notes that St. Louis adopted its FY2027 standards effective Jan 1, 2027 (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/52/topics/1301792-section-8-rents-went-up-for-fy2027-most-landlords-wont-collect-it). Out-of-state voucher landlords also struggle with local rules, as in a Cleveland thread on Section 8 inspection standards (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/963/topics/1302305-furnace-and-water-heater-on-wood-platforms-cleveland-section-8-inspection). A separate thread notes Section 8 tenants are 'already at maximum allowable rates' (https://www.biggerpockets.com/forums/963/topics/1302138-how-realistic-is-it-to-raise-rents-100-on-existing-tenants).
first_30_days: Week 1: hand-build payment-standard tables and request procedures for 3 housing authorities (start with St. Louis, Cleveland and Memphis). Publish a free calculator, 'How much did you leave on the table this year?', in the BiggerPockets Out-of-State and Landlording forums. Weeks 2 to 3: onboard 15 landlords, send requests manually with the templates, and track approvals. Week 4: turn on success-fee billing, and pitch 3 small voucher-heavy PM firms. Target: 15 landlords, 100+ units, and 10 documented approved increases.

title: Pre-Confirmation Screwworm Risk Feed for Cattle Markets
one_liner: A county-level early-warning feed that fuses news, vet reports, weather and zone announcements to give cattle buyers, auction barns and insurers days or weeks of lead time over official lab confirmation.
customer: Auction markets and sale barns, feedlots and stocker buyers, livestock lenders and insurers, and cattle-futures or ag-commodity desks. Ranchers and vet clinics are a low-price tier.
problem: New World screwworm has reached Texas and New Mexico. The UC San Diego team building a tracker says official reporting lags: 'Lab confirmation can take days or weeks.' Cattle prices, hauling rules and purchase decisions move on rumor and news before confirmation. Producers have no single source for zone status and their own exposure.
solution: A subscription feed that scores county-level risk from public and semi-public signals: state and APHIS zone announcements, extension and vet-clinic posts, local news, trap and case reports, and fly-friendly temperature and humidity. It sends SMS or email alerts and a plain-language 'movement readiness' checklist for each zone. Users can submit their own sightings, which improves the model. Sold in tiers from a $99/month producer plan to trading-desk contracts.
why_now: The screwworm reached the US Southwest in 2026, and APHIS newsroom items on 18 and 21 September 2026 show Texas releasing infested zones. The academic dashboard is a research tool, not a commercial product, and the sterile-fly response is slow to scale, so risk and compliance uncertainty will last through at least one fly season.
revenue_model: Producer and barn subscriptions at $99-500/month, insurer, lender and buyer contracts at $2-10k/month, and enterprise API fees for commodity desks.
non_obvious_insight: The academic value of the dashboard is the reporting lag itself: the UC San Diego team added media reports because 'lab confirmation can take days or weeks' (https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/09/260914102439.htm). The paying customer is anyone whose money moves on news before USDA confirms, meaning buyers, hedgers and insurers, not the county health officials the tool was built for. The lag is the product. Recent APHIS announcements show zone status is changing week to week (https://www.aphis.usda.gov/news).
first_30_days: Build a scraper and manual-curation pipeline over APHIS and Texas Animal Health Commission announcements, extension and vet feeds, and local news, plus a weather-based fly-activity index. Publish a free weekly map to gather emails. Pitch 10 sale barns and 3 commodity or insurer desks a paid pilot and sell the first 5 at a founding discount. Contact the UC San Diego team about a data and methods collaboration. Note that the APHIS screwworm page consulted in this session still said the pest was absent from the US, so confirm current case status before launch.

title: Protein Allocation Co-op for Mid-Size Brands
one_liner: A buyers' co-op that pools forward volume for whey and reformulates around shortages for brands too small to get allocation.
customer: Mid-size sports-nutrition, RTD beverage and bar brands (roughly $20-200M revenue) that lack direct cheese-plant relationships.
problem: Whey isolate is around $14/lb, some suppliers are sold out through 2026, and big buyers lock allocations, so small brands pay spot prices or get nothing.
solution: Aggregate members' forward demand into direct contracts with mid-size cheese and whey processors, and run a reformulation desk that blends whey with alternative proteins to spec.
why_now: The constraint is downstream whey-processing capacity and cheese output rather than raw milk, and factories are retooling for cottage cheese, so relationships and volume commitments now decide who gets protein.
revenue_model: Annual membership plus a 2-4% margin on pooled volume and fees for the reformulation desk.
non_obvious_insight: The shortage is partly a market-structure problem for small buyers rather than an absolute supply problem. Aggregation turns a set of unattractive small accounts into one large, plannable contract.
first_30_days: Recruit 8-10 brands into a founding cohort with combined tonnage, then hold calls with five mid-size cheese and whey plants to test whether they will commit capacity to a pooled buyer.

title: The True Acceptance Map for Rural Transfers
one_liner: Voice AI agents call every receiving psychiatric unit and specialty hospital each night to learn what they will actually accept, and rural ERs text a number to find out who will say yes.
customer: Critical access hospital EDs, state hospital associations and state rural health offices (paid with Rural Health Transformation Program funds), and state behavioral health authorities. Subscription per hospital or per state.
problem: A rural ER holding a suicidal 16-year-old, or a stroke, trauma or OB patient, may spend 3-8 hours making phone calls to place them. State bed registries say beds are open, but the real decision is made by a house supervisor at 2am applying unwritten rules: no IV drug history, no one-to-one sitter, no autism, no patients over 250 lb, no out-of-state Medicaid, no aggression, and no calls after 9pm without a physician-to-physician call. Every ER charge nurse keeps a battered binder or a phone note of who says yes to what and who to ask for. It lives in one head, and it goes out of date when a house supervisor changes.
solution: Use voice agents to call each facility's intake line on a schedule and extract structured, current answers: true open capacity by population, unwritten exclusions, insurance rules, the name and direct number of the person who decides, and the hours that person answers. Serve it back through a plain SMS interface. A nurse texts 'psych, 16yo, Medicaid, sitter needed, hx cutting' and gets a ranked call list with the exact script to use (the words that get an acceptance). Only facility rules are collected. No patient data is ever in the calls. Later, sell a receiving-side listing so facilities can pre-qualify referrals and get fewer dead-end calls.
why_now: Every state has now posted Rural Health Transformation Program funding opportunities (as of August 2026), and care coordination and access technology are core uses. Research on bed-tracking systems shows registries still leave clinicians phoning to check appropriateness, especially for aggressive, medically complex, autistic and dementia patients. Voice agents from 2025-26 can now hold a natural two-minute call with an intake nurse for a few cents. The workforce shortage means intake lines are answered by fewer people, which makes the tacit rules more valuable.
revenue_model: $300-600 per ER per month for SMS access. State-level licenses of $100-300k per year paid from RHTP or behavioral health funds. A second line is a receiving-facility listing at about $500 per month per facility. The proprietary asset is a data graph of real rules that no registry has.
non_obvious_insight: The valuable data is not bed counts, which are wrong within an hour. It is the tacit acceptance criteria and the identity of the human who decides, and it can only be learned by phone at night. That is why bed-registry vendors (built on hospital self-reporting) miss it. Facilities that discover their rules are being published accurately will cooperate, because a dead-end call costs them time too.
first_30_days: Pick one state or region. Type up the founder nurse's own binder, about 60-80 facilities, into a spreadsheet. Wire an off-the-shelf voice agent platform to call each facility nightly and write results to a table. Put an SMS bot in front of it with a Twilio number. Give it free to five ERs in the region and compare call counts and time to placement before and after. Bring the numbers to the state hospital association and the RHTP office.

title: Green-Claims Clearance for EU-Bound Brands
one_liner: A crawl-and-fix service that strips or substantiates banned 'eco-friendly' and 'climate-neutral' claims on packaging, product pages and ads for brands selling into the EU.
customer: DTC brands, Amazon and Shopify sellers, and mid-size consumer-goods companies selling to EU consumers, plus their marketing agencies and EU authorised representatives.
problem: Directive (EU) 2024/825 applies from 27 Sept 2026. It bans generic environmental claims ('green', 'eco-friendly') without recognised excellent performance, bans offset-based 'climate neutral' claims, and restricts sustainability labels to certified or public schemes. Small brands have thousands of SKUs of copy across 24 languages and no clear way to check it.
solution: Crawl product pages, packaging PDFs and ad libraries, flag banned and risky patterns in 24 languages, and suggest compliant rewrites with evidence-pack templates (life-cycle summary, certification proof). Add a human legal-review tier and monitoring of competitors' claims for complaint filing.
why_now: The rule began applying on 27 Sept 2026, and member-state transposition laws are now in force. The separate Green Claims Directive was shelved, so consultancies shifted attention, yet this ban is already law and cheap to police by machine.
revenue_model: $1-5k initial audit, $300-1,500 per month monitoring, and agency white-label licences.
non_obvious_insight: This is a deadline-driven, per-SKU checking problem that suits software plus a thin human legal layer, and the first enforcement will often start with competitor complaints. The best lead-gen is showing a brand its own violations.
first_30_days: Build a claims lexicon in five languages. Scan the top 200 product categories on Amazon.de and .fr for violations. Email brand founders their own violations as a free preview. Partner with three EU marketing agencies.

title: Pharma Load Attribution for EU Producer-Pays Wastewater
angle: Pairing 1: Aging/eldercare/silver economy x Water scarcity/infrastructure
one_liner: A neutral, audit-grade dataset showing which drugs from which producers, in which aging catchments and care homes, create the micropollutant load that EU pharma companies must now pay at least 80% of treatment for.
customer: National extended-producer-responsibility scheme operators and pharma/cosmetics trade bodies. Regional water boards and utilities deciding which large plants get quaternary treatment first also buy. Pricing is EUR 25-80k per study and EUR 100-250k a year for licenses.
problem: The recast Urban Wastewater Directive makes pharma and cosmetics producers fund at least 80% of quaternary treatment. The payment scheme is due by end-2028, and 20% of large plants must be upgraded by 2033. Annual cost estimates differ about 10x (EC EUR 1.2B, JRC EUR 1.56B, EurEau EUR 3.6-11.2B, Spain alone EUR 24.5B), and nobody owns the attribution of kilograms of active ingredient to payers. Older adults, care homes and hospitals are the concentrated source of medication residues, and Europe's 80+ cohort is its fastest-growing.
solution: A catchment-level model combining national dispensing statistics by age band, care-home and hospital bed registers, excretion and plant-removal rates, and receiving-water flow. It is validated by composite sampling at a handful of plants. It outputs load by active ingredient by plant, mapped to marketing-authorization-holder market shares for an allocation formula. A 'source-control screen' flags plants where pretreatment at a large care home or hospital removes more load per euro than plant-scale ozone or activated carbon, as a candidate for levy credits. The methodology is published so the scheme operator can defend it.
why_now: The directive is in transposition and the scheme design is being fought over now. The 10x cost disagreement means both utilities and producers need defensible numbers before 2028. European aging keeps raising per-capita medication load.
revenue_model: Per-study fees of EUR 25-80k for water boards. Annual licenses of EUR 100-250k to national scheme operators and industry associations for the allocation engine and yearly re-runs. Later, consulting on care-home source-control projects.
non_obvious_insight: The cost fight will be won by whoever supplies a referee-grade attribution dataset. The best predictor of load is not at the pipe but at the pillbox: age-structured dispensing and care-home density explain most of it. Demographics is the missing variable in water-quality economics, and neither water engineers nor pharma-market analysts hold both halves.
first_30_days: Start with the Netherlands and Germany, where open national dispensing statistics exist (for example the Dutch GIP databank). Model 5 mid-size catchments. Cold-pitch two regional water boards and one pharma producer association with the one-page result. Aim to close paid pilots at EUR 15-25k.

title: Buffet Lab: Hotel Breakfast Lines as Test Market
one_liner: Paid two-week trials that put reformulated or novel ingredients on real hotel and cruise breakfast lines, with item-level consumption, waste and hot-hold colour data.
customer: Food manufacturers facing the FDA petroleum-dye phase-out, and makers of natural colours and alternative proteins such as fermentation whey, rubisco and purple-sweet-potato colour, including farmer-owned processors. Hotels and cruise operators are the supply side.
problem: Dye reformulation costs $50K-$500K per SKU and takes 12-24+ months, and Walmart private label goes dye-free in January 2027. Whey is short and alt-protein funding has collapsed, so startups need cheap real-world proof. Lab sensory panels and retail test markets are slow, expensive and blind to failure modes like colour fade under lights, texture after hot-hold, and portion rejection by the roughly 12% of Americans on GLP-1s.
solution: Recruit 30-50 independent hotels plus one cruise or resort operator. Supply product free and track item-level consumption against control, plate waste, restock rates by daypart, QR feedback, hot-hold time and light exposure, with colorimeter photos of colour drift. Optionally A/B half-portions. Deliver a two-week acceptance, waste and stability report, and sell recurring access to the panel to CPG innovation teams.
why_now: The FDA dye phase-out targets December 2027, with 22 states adding food-restriction rules and a federal ultra-processed food definition in review. Whey concentrate is up 108% in two years, alt-protein funding fell to $881M in 2025 with only $197M in H1 2026, and GLP-1 users are reshaping portions and protein preferences. Buyers want supply-risk answers, not sustainability stories.
revenue_model: $12K-$30K per product trial. Hotels receive product, about $40/day and waste analytics. Panel subscriptions for CPG innovation teams of $60K-$120K/yr.
non_obvious_insight: A hotel breakfast line is the largest measurable eating experiment in commerce: repeat business travellers, captive choice, fixed hot-hold time and lighting, and a natural weigh-back at clearing. It stress-tests exactly the things that kill natural-colour and protein reformulations, much faster than a retail test market.
first_30_days: Recruit 8 independent hotels via an owners' association and approach 5 natural-colour and ingredient startups directly. Run one paid pilot, for example a dye-free pastry glaze or cereal, at about $8K to prove the report format.

title: Transition Sponsor Radar for Strategic Breakthrough Awards
one_liner: A subscription and dossier service that maps each SBIR Phase II technology to the specific budget line, program office and person who could commit to a Program Objective Memorandum (POM), which the new $30M Strategic Breakthrough awards require.
customer: Phase II awardees in DoD-funded SBIR (thousands per year) that want Phase III or Strategic Breakthrough money, plus SBIR-focused VCs and advisors who decide which portfolio companies to back.
problem: Strategic Breakthrough awards run up to $30M over 48 months, but a company needs at least one prior Phase II, at least 100% matching funds from new private capital or non-SBIR government money, and, for DoD, a 'commitment for inclusion in a program objective memorandum' from the acquisition executive or higher. Agencies must contract within 90 days of a proposal. The technology is rarely the bottleneck. The bottleneck is finding the one person with authority over a budget line, and knowing the POM calendar, since the POM is written 18 to 24 months ahead of the fiscal year. The public data (R-1/R-2 RDT&E exhibits, P-1 procurement lines, FPDS contracts, SBIR.gov awards) exists but is not indexed by technology.
solution: Build a searchable graph linking SBIR.gov Phase II abstracts to R-2 program elements, project numbers and named PEOs/PMs, and to FPDS Phase III contracts (where SBIR data-rights clauses appear). For each customer, produce a 'sponsor dossier': the top 5 program elements that could absorb the tech, the POM cycle dates, who to call, precedent Phase III transitions, and candidate match-fund sources. Add a monthly alert when a relevant program element grows or a new Phase III model contract appears.
why_now: The Strategic Breakthrough allocation (up to 0.50% of an agency's R&D budget where R&D exceeds $100M) takes effect in FY2026 and runs to September 30, 2031. Agencies must also create standardized Phase I/II/III model contracts and track direct-to-Phase-II, strategic breakthrough and Phase III awards in the database. Data on where transitions happen will become far richer as this reporting starts.
revenue_model: $12k to $20k per tech-specific sponsor dossier, paid partly from the $50k Phase II T&BA allowance. $1,500 per month subscription for alerts and updates. $5k per month for SBIR-focused VC funds screening deals. Success fee on Phase III wins (1% to 3%) as an optional add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is not funding, it is a named budget-holder who will put a line in a POM, and that map is buildable from public documents no one has joined to SBIR data. S. 3971 Section 3 (new Section 9(ff)(3)) sets the $30M cap, 48-month term, one prior Phase II, 100% match, DoD POM-commitment requirement and 90-day contracting deadline. Section 6 requires 'simplified and standardized procedures and model contracts' for Phase III. Section 8 requires the database to track Phase III prime and subcontract awards. All at https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/BILLS-119s3971enr/html/BILLS-119s3971enr.htm. The award-size thresholds the SBA gave for April 2026 ($323,090 Phase I, $2,153,927 Phase II without SBA approval, https://www.sbir.gov/about) show how small the normal awards are next to a $30M award, so the sponsor commitment becomes the step everyone is scrambling for.
first_30_days: Download the SBIR.gov awards dataset and the latest DoD RDT&E R-2 exhibits (comptroller.defense.gov). Use an LLM to embed and match 200 recent Phase II abstracts to program elements, then have a former acquisition officer sanity-check the top matches. Give 10 Phase II founders a free one-page 'sponsor map' for their own tech. Convert 3 of them to a $12k dossier. Pitch 2 SBIR-focused VC funds a paid pilot on their portfolio.

title: 90-Day Bridge Power for Robotaxi Depots
one_liner: Containerized battery-buffered charging stalls leased per stall per month so AV fleets can open depots years before the utility connects them.
customer: Robotaxi fleet operators and depot managers, autonomous-truck terminals, and electric delivery-van fleets that need charging capacity fast.
problem: Depot power is the scaling choke point. California lead times run about 6 months for a standard charging site, 1.9 years for a new circuit, 2.8 years for a substation upgrade and 8.9 years for a new substation, and depots compete with data centers for powered industrial land. Waymo alone has 3,871 vehicles and is aiming much higher.
solution: Modular systems combining second-life EV battery storage, a small grid tie (200-500 kW) and charging software that schedules vehicles around available energy. Sell 'stalls online in 90 days' as power-as-a-service. When the full grid connection arrives, the same assets convert to peak shaving and grid-services revenue.
why_now: Waymo, Tesla and Zoox (charging fares since August 10, 2026) are all scaling at once, and interconnection queues now outrun vehicle deployment. Data-center bridge power has proven that customers will pay a premium for time-to-power.
revenue_model: $600-1,000 per stall per month, or $0.30-0.45 per kWh delivered, on 3-5 year contracts, with asset financing behind them.
non_obvious_insight: For AV scale-up the binding constraint is interconnection time, not vehicles or software. Turning 'megawatts in two years' into 'kilowatts now, megawatts later' beats the utility's queue, and buffered assets keep earning after the grid arrives.
first_30_days: Get an LOI for a 20-stall pilot from one depot operator or delivery-van fleet. Source used battery modules through a reseller and integrate an existing containerized storage vendor's hardware rather than building your own. Target first revenue in month 4.

title: Multi-Rail Cash-Flow Underwriting After UPI Fees
one_liner: When UPI stops being free for big tickets, reconstruct small-merchant revenue from GST, bank and supplier data instead of UPI alone.
customer: NBFCs, small finance banks and cash-flow lenders that lend to kirana and small retail businesses.
problem: Lenders assumed UPI data was the universal truth for underwriting. The Oct 15 MDR (0.4% above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300) hits about 4% of P2M volume but about 66% of value, so merchants now have a reason to route big tickets through cash or bank transfer.
solution: An API that combines Account Aggregator bank data, GST e-invoice and filing data, supplier invoices and soundbox/QR data into a revenue estimate with a rail-shift adjustment. The wedge is a turnover sanity-check score for five NBFCs.
why_now: MDR starts Oct 15, the Supreme Court refused a stay, and retailers are organising protests. RBI's cash-flow lending push depends on this data.
revenue_model: Rs 40-120 per scored application plus a monitoring fee on the live loan book.
non_obvious_insight: A fee on exactly the high-value 66% creates an incentive to hide it. The rail shift is a data-quality shock, and the first lender to model it gets an underwriting edge.
first_30_days: Get consented data on about 200 existing borrowers from one NBFC partner and backtest against repayments. Offer a 60-day free pilot.

title: Short-Time Compensation as a Service
one_liner: Software and admin that lets employers shrink hours instead of headcount using state work-sharing programs, where unemployment insurance replaces part of the lost wages, as an alternative to AI-driven layoffs.
customer: HR and finance leaders at 50-2,000-employee firms in states with work-sharing programs (about half of US states, verify) planning 10-30% reductions in AI-exposed teams. PEOs and payroll providers are channels.
problem: Employers treat headcount cuts as binary, yet many states pay prorated UI when firms cut hours 10-60% rather than lay people off. Almost nobody uses it. AI-driven demand shifts are gradual and uncertain, layoffs risk rehire regret and severance costs, and workers lose health coverage and face 6-13 month searches.
solution: (1) A calculator comparing work-sharing to layoff, including severance, recruiting and regret costs. (2) Plan-filing automation per state. (3) Weekly claim administration integrated with payroll. (4) A training-hours module for reduced-hours periods. (5) Tracking of approvals and caps. (6) A glide path to natural attrition.
why_now: AI restructuring is happening under uncertainty (Challenger shows AI-cited cuts small and partly narrative), reversal headlines are growing, and the market is low-fire, low-hire, so retaining talent has become valuable.
revenue_model: $25-60 per participating employee per month, or 5-10% of validated avoided severance and rehire cost, plus PEO reseller revenue.
non_obvious_insight: The subsidy already exists and is unused because nobody owns the admin burden. Becoming the 'TurboTax for work-sharing' turns a public benefit into a retention and anti-regret hedge that contradicts the 'cut now' reflex.
first_30_days: Map work-sharing rules and forms in the 6-8 biggest states. Interview 15 mid-size HR leads and 5 PEOs. Offer free feasibility analyses to companies that filed WARN notices and convert 2-3 to paid pilots.

title: Reserve-Crew Backup Photographers for Wedding Day Emergencies
one_liner: A paid-standby bench of pre-vetted, style-matched backup photographers who can be dispatched within 2-3 hours, sold to solo photographers as a subscription and to wedding insurers as claims fulfillment.
customer: Solo and small-studio wedding photographers ($199-399/yr for a 'Continuity Guarantee' they can promise couples), plus wedding-insurance carriers and MGAs that cover vendor failure but cannot produce a person.
problem: Every solo photographer's nightmare is a sudden illness, crash or family emergency six hours before a wedding. The standard backup plan in contracts is 'a photographer friend', which fails in practice. On peak Saturdays (dates like 10/10/26) every competent local shooter is already booked, so the Facebook SOS post at 6am gets 40 sympathetic comments and zero style-matched, available humans. Whoever does show up has never seen the timeline, venue notes, family-formals list or the photographer's look. Wedding insurance reimburses money after the fact but cannot supply a competent human in three hours. It is a capacity-reservation problem, not an insurance problem.
solution: Members upload style samples plus a 'Continuity Pack' for each booked wedding (timeline, family list, venue and light notes, gallery drop link), all in one place. We maintain a regional bench of vetted shooters tagged by style (documentary, bright and airy, moody, film-look). Bench shooters are paid a small standby retainer (about $40) to hold peak dates, plus an activation fee ($500-900) paid by the member or the insurer. On activation, the pack is pushed to the understudy, a coordinator handles couple communication, and images are delivered under the member's brand. Members display a 'Continuity Guaranteed' badge, which becomes a booking-conversion asset.
why_now: Vendor-failure cover is now a standard add-on in wedding insurance, and 2026 contracts increasingly require a comparable replacement or a full refund, so the gap between reimbursing money and supplying a photographer is now visible and contractual. Weekend supply is squeezed onto peak dates, and a growing pool of freelance portrait, real-estate and second-shooter talent with open weekends can be organized cheaply through Stripe Connect and shared workspaces. Insurers are also under pressure to reduce claim severity in small commercial lines.
revenue_model: $99-399/yr member subscription (tiered by number of weddings), per-activation fee split with the bench shooter (we keep about 20%), and an insurer contract of a flat per-policy fee or per-claim fulfillment fee. Standby retainers are funded from the subscription pool, like airline reserve crews.
non_obvious_insight: Backup fails precisely on the dates it is needed, because scarcity is correlated. The free 'photographer friend' network evaporates on peak Saturdays. The only fix is paying for reserved capacity in advance, and once you do, you own the only reliable answer to the industry's most feared event.
first_30_days: Pick one metro. Sign 25 solo photographers as founding members at $99/yr and recruit 8 bench shooters (portrait, real-estate and second-shooter talent with open Saturdays). Build the Continuity Pack in Notion/Airtable plus a shared Google Drive. Run a fire drill: on a chosen Saturday, ping every member's pack and time how fast each is delivered to a bench shooter. Pitch two wedding-insurance MGAs on a 90-day claims-fulfillment pilot, and get a lawyer to check contractor and liability terms before the first live activation.

title: Supplier Divorce Protection: Tool Census and Overrun Forensics
one_liner: When a US manufacturer leaves a Chinese contract manufacturer, we find out which molds and dies it really owns, and prove whether the ex-supplier is still running them off the books.
customer: US OEMs and PE-owned manufacturers ($50M-$500M revenue) that moved or are moving injection-molded, die-cast, stamped or extruded product out of China within the last 24 months, and hold $200k-$5M of tooling there. The buyer is the COO or VP Supply Chain, with General Counsel as co-signer. General counsel and brand-protection managers are the second buyer.
problem: Most small and mid-size OEMs cannot say which tools they own, where they physically sit, or what condition they are in. The paper trail is a PO line item from 2016 and a WeChat thread. When the relationship ends, the supplier slow-walks tool release, demands storage or release fees, and sometimes runs overruns on your tooling on a third shift and sells them to distributors and marketplaces at a discount. You then compete against your own product, and lawyers cannot help because nobody can prove which tool made which part.
solution: Three stacked products. (1) Tool Census: a local partner audits each supplier on video and in person, laser-tags every tool with a serial, records its condition and appraised value, and captures a macro-photo 'fingerprint' library of each cavity (gate vestige, ejector-pin witness marks, texture flaws, parting-line signature). (2) Overrun Watch: monitor Amazon, Alibaba, 1688, Temu, eBay and Walmart Marketplace for look-alike parts, buy samples, and match them to cavity fingerprints, date wheels and lot codes with computer-vision-assisted forensics. That yields evidence packs for marketplace takedowns, CBP IPR recordation, or counsel. (3) Tool Extraction: negotiate release, handle Chinese export paperwork and freight, and re-qualify the tool in Ohio.
why_now: The Reshoring Initiative's 2026 survey shows 36% of OEMs reshored this year, up from 29%. The 2025 tariff whiplash ended a lot of Chinese supplier relationships, and the Feb 2026 Supreme Court IEEPA ruling is now churning sourcing decisions again, so the number of messy breakups is at a peak. Cheap macro-imaging and vision models make tool-mark matching, previously an expensive forensic-lab exercise, feasible at SMB prices.
revenue_model: Tool Census at $6k-$15k per supplier site. Overrun Watch at $2k-$5k per month per product family. Forensic evidence pack at $3k-$8k per case. Extraction at 8-12% of appraised tool value plus pass-through freight. Expected first-year ACV per client is $40k-$120k.
non_obvious_insight: Outsiders think IP loss in China means someone copies your design. Insiders know the far bigger leak is your own paid-for tool running unrecorded shifts, and that every cavity is a physical fingerprint the supplier cannot deny. Ownership of the tooling is the real leverage in any break-up, and almost nobody documents it until the day they need it.
first_30_days: Skip China operations at first. Sell a remote $2,500 'Marketplace Overrun Audit': buy 10 units of the client's product from 1688, Alibaba and Temu, compare them to the golden sample and lot codes, and deliver a one-page verdict. Sign 3 design partners through Ohio plant-manager and Reshoring Initiative networks, and line up a Dongguan or Ningbo audit contractor by referral. Book a one-hour consult with an IP litigator who will white-label the evidence-pack format.

title: ITAR-Safe Identity for New-Space Startups
angle: Pairing 2: Space economy x Cybersecurity/identity fraud (identity verification and hiring fraud)
one_liner: An identity layer that proves a new hire is real, where they actually are and whether they may legally see spacecraft technical data, then feeds that attribute straight into SSO and PLM access controls.
customer: Series A-C launch, satellite and defense-space startups (50-500 staff) and their sub-tier machine shops and avionics suppliers, reached through space-focused investors, accelerators and SpaceWERX/SBIR cohorts. Buyers are the head of security or compliance and the CFO.
problem: Space startups are hiring at breakneck speed, with remote engineers and contractors, into a Golden Dome-driven market (cost estimate raised to $185B) and nine-figure funding rounds. Giving a foreign person access to technical data is an ITAR export violation, and North Korean IT-worker schemes have reached 70 to 100+ US companies. Standard IDV proves someone is real, not whether they are a US person, and HR and ATS tools do not carry export-control eligibility as an access attribute. Fake suppliers and counterfeit parts add a second exposure.
solution: (1) Verify person and US-person status using document and injection-resistant liveness (partner with an existing IDV vendor rather than building it). (2) Check presence over time (VPN and laptop-farm signals). (3) Write 'US person, permitted data categories' into Okta or Entra groups and PLM and repo permissions through SCIM. (4) Supplier onboarding with KYB, sanctions and counterfeit-part red flags. (5) An auditor-ready evidence pack for CMMC Level 2 assessments and export-compliance reviews.
why_now: The DoD's CMMC rollout reaches its second phase on 10 Nov 2026, when third-party Level 2 certification starts appearing in contracts, and small suppliers are scrambling. North Korean worker prosecutions in Apr and May 2026 put hiring fraud on boards' agendas, while 3-second voice cloning and virtual-camera injection attacks defeat casual video interviews.
revenue_model: $60-120 per verified person per year, $1-3K per month platform fee, and $250 per supplier onboarding. Add a paid $2K 'ITAR access audit' as an entry product.
non_obvious_insight: In space the compliance object is not employee identity but nationality-scoped access to technical data. The unbuilt gap is attribute-based access control fed by identity proof into CAD and PLM systems. These startups fear DDTC and DoD audits and investor diligence more than hackers, so they buy compliance evidence rather than security.
first_30_days: Build a 'verified US person to Okta group' integration on an off-the-shelf IDV API. Sell a $2K ITAR access audit (export the Drive, GitHub and PLM permission lists and flag foreign-person exposures) to 5 startups via investor and accelerator introductions in Colorado Springs, Los Angeles and Huntsville. Convert audits to per-seat subscriptions before the Nov 2026 CMMC milestone.

title: Bonded Escorts for Sedated Outpatient Patients
one_liner: A background-checked adult who legally receives your discharge instructions and takes you home after a colonoscopy or other sedated procedure, sold to the clinics that lose the slot when you have no ride.
customer: Independent GI groups and ambulatory surgery centers pay $65-95 per escorted visit. Solo agers and estranged or far-from-family adults pay $99-149 directly as a fallback.
problem: Most sedation centers will not proceed unless a responsible adult picks the patient up and hears the discharge instructions, and many refuse to release a sedated patient to a rideshare driver. Patients with no spouse, no nearby family, or no friend willing to sit through the aftermath of a bowel prep cancel, delay screening, or no-show. The clinic eats an empty high-margin slot. The patient feels embarrassed to ask and avoids the procedure.
solution: A regional network of vetted, insured escorts drawn from CNAs, retired nurses, EMTs and nursing students. The clinic scheduler adds one line to the booking call: 'No escort? Tap here and we will send one.' The escort meets the patient at the door, is named on the chart as the responsible adult, receives instructions, rides home with the patient, stays 20-30 minutes until the patient is settled, and texts a family contact. A clinic dashboard shows escort confirmed, so day-of cancellations for this reason disappear. Later add the required 24-hour post-anesthesia overnight companion, then cataract, oral surgery, and cosmetic and orthopedic day surgery.
why_now: The USPSTF lowered the colorectal screening start age to 45, which added millions of eligible patients. Procedures keep migrating to ambulatory surgery centers, which run on tight slot economics. The share of older adults living alone (solo agers) is at a record high. Checkr-style vetting and Stripe Connect-style payouts let a tiny team stand up a bonded, insured gig network in weeks. No incumbent sells 'the adult on the chart' to schedulers.
revenue_model: Per-visit fee paid by the clinic ($65-95, escort keeps about 60%) or patient-pay ($99-149). Add-ons include overnight post-anesthesia sitters billed hourly. Later, Medicare Advantage plans buy escort-with-transport as a supplemental benefit.
non_obvious_insight: The escort rule is a liability policy, not a medical one, so what the clinic needs is a credentialed name on the chart that satisfies the discharge nurse, not a ride. Nobody sells to the scheduling desk, where the cancellation leak is measured in dollars per slot. The patient's real barrier is shame at asking a friend to witness a colonoscopy, which a professional stranger removes.
first_30_days: Pick one metro. Recruit 15 escorts from nursing-school boards and retired-nurse groups. Get a general and professional liability quote and run Checkr checks. Visit 10 GI practices and offer a free 30-day pilot where they pay only when an escort saves a slot that would have cancelled. Launch a landing page and a Twilio text line, and buy Google Ads on searches like 'colonoscopy no one to drive me home'. Run dispatch from a spreadsheet. Goal: 40 escorted procedures and 3 signed clinics.

title: Reproduction-Gated Vulnerability Inbox for Maintainers
one_liner: A hosted security-report intake that only forwards a report if its proof-of-concept actually reproduces against the maintainer's tagged release in a sandbox, so AI-generated slop dies before a human reads it.
customer: Maintainers and foundations of widely depended-on open-source projects (paid by corporate sponsors and dependents), plus small vendors that must run a coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy under the CRA. They pay $99-499/month per project, or $2k/month sponsor-funded shields for critical projects.
problem: curl ended its bug bounty at the end of January 2026 to 'remove the incentive for people to submit crap and non-well researched reports... AI generated or not'; in the week before, 7 submissions contained no real vulnerabilities but still burned security-team time. Maintainers are also drowning in PRs, with Ladybird banning non-maintainer PRs and Rust's Clippy gamifying review, while companies float donating AI credits to maintainers instead.
solution: An intake form and GitHub App that requires a machine-checkable reproducer (Dockerfile/script/HTTP request plus the expected oracle, such as an ASAN crash, unexpected file read or assertion). The service builds the project at the reported tag in a microVM, runs the reproducer and only escalates reports that trip the oracle. Failures get instant automated feedback. Passing reports arrive at the maintainer as a verified repro bundle, deduplicated against past reports, with a suggested severity and a drafted advisory and CVE request. Logic bugs without automatic oracles go through a refundable deposit lane. Start with memory-safety classes (C/C++/Rust/Go) where oracles are objective.
why_now: January 2026 made the AI-slop-versus-security-report problem concrete and public. CRA reporting duties began in September 2026, increasing report volume and the need for a documented intake. Cheap microVM sandboxes (Firecracker-class) make per-report verification cost cents.
revenue_model: Sponsor-paid subscriptions: $99-499/month per project, funded by the top dependents (companies that already say they want to help maintainers, per the AI-credits thread). $1-2k/month for critical projects. Per-verified-report fee for small vendors with public VDPs.
non_obvious_insight: Everyone argues about banning submissions or paying for them; nobody has moved the burden of proof onto machines, and the same LLMs that write slop cannot fake a crashing sanitizer trace on the maintainer's own build. The buyer is not the burned-out maintainer with no budget but the dependents who need that maintainer to keep going. Evidence: curl closing its bounty https://www.theregister.com/2026/01/21/curl_ends_bug_bounty/; maintainers asking how to handle PR slop and pointing to tools https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47492078; Ladybird and Clippy approaches plus a call for third-party solutions https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48949019; companies wanting to donate but debating the wrong instrument (credits vs money) https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48346013.
first_30_days: Build the GitHub App and intake page for C, Rust and Go projects using sanitizer/crash oracles. Recruit 3 mid-size maintainers by replying in the PR-slop and AI-contribution Ask HN threads; run their real inbox through it in shadow mode for two weeks and report the percentage of reports filtered. Take that data to each project's top corporate dependents and ask for a $250/month sponsorship that funds the shield.

title: LOMA Rescue for Newly Flood-Mapped Homeowners
one_liner: Door-to-door service that gets newly mapped flood-zone homeowners an elevation certificate and a FEMA map amendment (LOMA) package before they are forced into flood insurance, with surveyors paying for the leads.
customer: Homeowners whose parcels were just moved into FEMA high-risk zones, who pay $600-900 for an elevation certificate plus filing. Licensed surveyors pay $75-150 per booked job, and private flood MGAs pay referral fees for owners who do not qualify.
problem: Thousands of homes were newly mapped into Special Flood Hazard Areas. Mandatory purchase kicks in fast, and change notification is not mandatory, so many owners learn from a lender letter. Many do not know that a home whose lowest adjacent grade sits above the base flood elevation can petition out. A one-time survey cost competes with a permanent premium annuity plus escrow increases.
solution: A parcel-level tracker of FEMA map-change communities, with screening from public elevation and LiDAR data. We mail and door-hang targeted homeowners with a fixed-price 'get out or get covered' offer. We book a vetted surveyor, file the LOMA package, and route non-qualifiers straight to private flood quotes (referral fee) and mitigation contractors.
why_now: Cotality reports (2026-09-18) that new FEMA maps put thousands of homes into high-risk zones across 100+ communities in 12 states. Homeowners must secure cover within 45 days, and for 10% of homeowners escrow already exceeds principal and interest. NOAA's flood inundation mapping reached nearly 100% of the US population in September 2026, which raises public awareness of flood exposure.
revenue_model: Flat $700-1,000 homeowner package split with the surveyor (about 25-30% margin), plus $50-150 referral fees on private flood or NFIP binds for non-qualifiers. Later sold as a white-label to title companies and community lenders.
non_obvious_insight: The 'uninsurable' problem is here solved by contesting the map, not by finding a carrier. Evidence from https://www.carriermanagement.com/news/2026/09/18/292073.htm: the top newly mapped communities are Escambia County FL (2,344 properties), Pender County NC (678), Chattanooga TN (635), Ithaca NY (428) and Methuen MA (428). The article says change notifications are not mandatory, leaving some homeowners uninformed, and that homeowners have 45 days to secure flood insurance. About 4,500 named parcels in five communities is a concrete addressable list with a hard deadline and no dominant consumer-facing service. Only owners with grade above base flood elevation qualify, so the model needs screening and an honest fallback.
first_30_days: Pull the parcel lists for the five named communities from county GIS and FEMA change notices. Pre-screen elevations with public LiDAR. Sign 2 local licensed surveyors on per-job pricing. Mail 1,000 letters or door hangers in Escambia and Pender with a fixed price and a free eligibility check. Target 20-30 booked certificates in the first month.

title: Certified SDE for Sub-$1M Business Sales
one_liner: A CPA-signed, AI-prepared earnings certificate that lets brokers, buyers and SBA lenders trust a small business's seller's discretionary earnings.
customer: Business brokers, SBA lenders and first-time buyers in $100k-$1M main-street deals, and the sellers who pay to be believed.
problem: A full quality-of-earnings review costs $15-50k, which is impossible on a $300k deal, so cash-heavy books and owner add-backs create distrust. Deals die in diligence or stall in lender underwriting. Search funds target $5-50M businesses and nothing standardizes trust for the smallest tier.
solution: Upload three years of returns, bank and processor statements and POS data. The system reconstructs revenue, recasts SDE with add-back evidence, and flags unrecorded revenue or personal expenses. A CPA signs a certified SDE range in 48 hours. Partner lenders accept the standard report, and it links to the escrow and route-sale flow.
why_now: SBA 7(a) plus 504 financing up to $10M began July 2026, so buyer demand and lender appetite are rising. LLMs and bank data make the reconstruction cheap.
revenue_model: $495-995 per report paid by the seller or broker, lender licensing, and buyer diligence upsells.
non_obvious_insight: At this size the bottleneck is neither buyers nor capital but trust in the earnings number. A QoE costs 5% of price, and a cheap certificate unlocks the whole tier.
first_30_days: Sign three brokers who list $200k-800k deals and produce 15 reports manually with a CPA. Ask one SBA lender in writing what it needs in order to accept the certificate.

title: Lot-Level Verification for Generic Semaglutide Importers
one_liner: A shared-API lineage database plus independent identity and impurity testing for distributors and pharmacy chains buying the flood of post-patent generic semaglutide.
customer: Distributors, pharmacy chains, hospital groups and telehealth clinics in India, Canada, Brazil and the 75+ markets Indian exporters like Hetero now target, and payers or regulators who need lot-level evidence.
problem: Semaglutide patents lapsed in Canada (Jan 2026), India and Brazil (Mar 2026), and 40+ Indian companies launched brands within weeks. By July, Dr. Reddy's halted supply through at least late October over an API impurity, and Torrent recalled Semalix batches after Dr. Reddy's notice because it uses the same API. Buyers can't see which brands share which API source, and fake pens circulate.
solution: Build an API-lineage graph from customs and shipping records, regulatory notices, recalls and public dossiers, mapping each brand and batch to its API manufacturer, and alert subscribers when any brand in the shared-API cluster has an event. Pair this with fast lot testing (LC-MS peptide identity and purity, impurity profile) through accredited partner labs in India, the UAE and Brazil, returning a signed 'verified lot' certificate with QR lookup. Start with a free public recall-radar page and newsletter to collect buyers.
why_now: Generics launched in March-July 2026 across three large markets at once (India prices as low as Rs 1,500 a month), regulators are stretched, and the first recalls and counterfeit guidance are already published. Tirzepatide and US semaglutide remain patented, so the gray market will keep growing alongside the legitimate one.
revenue_model: $250-$600 per verified lot, $500-$2,000 a month for lineage alerts and API access, and custom supplier audits for hospital groups and exporters.
non_obvious_insight: Forty-plus brands is not forty-plus independent risks: a handful of API sources means one impurity event propagates across supposedly competing brands, and no buyer-side tool maps that. Evidence: BusinessLine's headline 'DRL's semaglutide supply hits a stumbling block, affects other companies too' and Economic Times' Torrent recall after Dr. Reddy's notice (Jul 9, 2026) via Google News (https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=Torrent+Semalix+recall+Dr+Reddy%27s+API+semaglutide+Canada); Fierce Pharma on the pause (https://www.fiercepharma.com/manufacturing/dr-reddys-presses-pause-generic-semaglutide-supply-after-flagging-api-issue). India Today: 'Quality concerns hit cheap Ozempic copies in India within months'. NDTV, Mar 30, 2026: 'How To Spot Fakes'. Hetero: 1.5M pens, 75+ markets (Medical Dialogues Apr 16, 2026). Patent-expiry dates and 40-50 brands: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semaglutide.
first_30_days: Days 1-7: assemble a public database of every Indian semaglutide brand, the marketing-authorization holder, contract manufacturer and any disclosed API source, and ship the recall-radar page. Days 7-20: sign a testing-lab partner in India or the UAE on a wholesale per-lot price, and run 20 lots bought retail as a published 'state of the market' report. Days 20-30: pitch 25 importers, pharmacy chains and telehealth clinics with a free lineage check plus a $400 lot test, and aim for 5 paid tests.

title: Refundable Deposits Against AI Submission Floods
one_liner: A gateway that makes AI-generated reports, applications and pitches post a small refundable stake, so maintainers only read submissions someone bet on.
customer: Open-source maintainers and foundations, bug-bounty program owners, and other inboxes overwhelmed by AI-generated submissions (journals, grant makers, VC and press inboxes, public-comment portals). Start with OSS security teams and mid-size bounty programs.
problem: curl scrapped its bug bounty in January 2026 after valid reports fell below 5%, and its maintainer floated an entrance fee. HackerOne reportedly paused its Internet Bug Bounty in March after a 76% year-on-year jump in submissions, and other projects have retired bounties. Agents removed the effort-based backpressure open-source governance relied on. Content classifiers lose the arms race to models that write plausible reports.
solution: A stake API and form: the submitter (human or agent) posts a refundable deposit of $5-$50 by card or machine payment. Triage marks the report valid (refund plus any bounty) or invalid (deposit goes to maintainers or charity). Integrations for GitHub Security Advisories, email intake and bounty-platform webhooks. Reporters with track records get deposit discounts, and unpaid stakes flow to the program.
why_now: The curl and HackerOne events are recent and public. Machine Payments Protocol (March 2026) and card rails make small, programmatic deposits practical, and agents now file at scale.
revenue_model: 10-15% of forfeited deposits plus $99-$499/month per program for triage tooling, with sponsor-funded tiers for open-source projects.
non_obvious_insight: Price is the only filter that scales with attacker capacity. An agent must risk money on every claim, honest reporters get refunded, so the cost lands only on slop. Postage as a spam filter failed when senders were humans, but agent-operated senders have budgets and ROI math.
first_30_days: Build a GitHub Security Advisory plus web-form integration in two weeks. Recruit 5 OSS projects that have publicly complained and run a 30-day pilot measuring valid-report rate. Then approach bounty platforms with the data.
